title: C-Level & Boardroom
completion_message: ¡Soberbio! Acabas de aprender el vocabulario exacto que se usa en las salas de juntas (boardrooms) al más alto nivel corporativo. Ya estás listo para hablar como un CEO.

stages.title: Vocabulario C-Level y de Sala de Juntas

parts.visual:
Términos Corporativos de Alto Nivel: 
- C-Suite / C-Level (Los altos ejecutivos: CEO, CFO, CTO, COO). 
Ej: The C-Suite is having a meeting right now. 
- Board of Directors (Junta Directiva). 
Ej: The board of directors approved the merger. 
- Hostile takeover (Adquisición hostil / Comprar una empresa en contra de la voluntad de su dirección). 
Ej: They launched a hostile takeover of the rival company.
parts.audio: High-Level Corporate Terms. 'C-Suite' or 'C-Level' refers to the top executives like the C E O, C F O, and C T O. For example: The C-Suite is having a meeting right now. The 'Board of Directors' is the group of people elected to represent shareholders. For example: The board of directors approved the merger. A 'Hostile takeover' is when a company is bought against the wishes of its management. For example: They launched a hostile takeover of the rival company.

parts.visual:
Acuerdos y Compensaciones: 
- Golden parachute (Paracaídas dorado / Gran compensación financiera garantizada a un ejecutivo si es despedido). 
Ej: The CEO left with a $10 million golden parachute. 
- Monopolize (Monopolizar / Tener control total). 
Ej: They are trying to monopolize the market. 
- Redundancy / Layoffs (Despidos masivos por falta de trabajo/fondos). 
Ej: The company announced 500 redundancies.
parts.audio: Agreements and Compensations. A 'Golden parachute' is a huge financial compensation guaranteed to an executive if they are fired. For example: The C E O left with a 10 million dollar golden parachute. To 'Monopolize' means to have total control over a market. For example: They are trying to monopolize the market. 'Redundancy' or 'Layoffs' refer to mass firings usually due to a lack of funds or work. For example: The company announced 500 redundancies.

stages.title: Interactive Quiz
stages.description: Elige el término C-Level correcto para cada situación ejecutiva.

questions.question: The top executives in a company (CEO, CFO, CTO) are known collectively as the ____. (Ejecutivos de nivel C).
The ____ of Directors meets every quarter to discuss the company's strategy. (Junta Directiva).
They bought the company against the wishes of its management. It was a ____ takeover. (Adquisición hostil).
questions.explanation: Hostile takeover = toma de control u OPA hostil.

questions.question: Even though he was fired for poor performance, he left with a $5 million ____ parachute. (Paracaídas dorado).
questions.explanation: Golden parachute = indemnización millonaria para altos ejecutivos.

questions.question: Because of the economic crisis, the company announced massive ____. (Despidos masivos).
questions.explanation: Layoffs / Redundancies = despidos por recortes de personal.

questions.question: The new law prevents large tech companies from trying to ____ the market. (Monopolizar).
A ____ company is a company that is completely owned by another company. (Subsidiaria/Filial).
The company that owns the subsidiary is called the ____ company. (Empresa matriz).
The board decided to ____ the CEO because of the recent scandal. (Destituir / Expulsar).
questions.explanation: Oust = destituir, expulsar de un cargo de poder.

questions.question: When two companies join together to form a new company, it is called a ____. (Fusión).
When one company buys another, it is called an ____. (Adquisición).
We are looking for a highly ____ executive to lead the new department. (Capacitado / De alto nivel).
questions.explanation: A seasoned executive = un ejecutivo experimentado/veterano.

questions.question: The CEO has the final say, but he usually consults his ____ of advisors. (Círculo íntimo).
questions.explanation: Inner circle = círculo íntimo o de confianza.

questions.question: We need to do our ____ diligence before buying that company. (Diligencia debida / Auditoría previa).
questions.explanation: Due diligence = auditoría o investigación exhaustiva antes de una firma/compra.

questions.question: The company was accused of ____ trading (using secret information to buy stocks). (Uso de información privilegiada).
questions.explanation: Insider trading = tráfico de información privilegiada.

questions.question: The ____ line of this report is that we are losing money. (Conclusión / Resultado final).
questions.explanation: The bottom line = el resultado neto, la conclusión principal.

questions.question: They made a ____ bid to buy the company for $500 million. (Oferta pública de adquisición).
A ____ is someone who reveals illegal activities happening within their company. (Denunciante).
questions.explanation: Whistleblower = informante, denunciante de prácticas corruptas.

questions.question: The executives met in the ____ to discuss the confidential strategy. (Sala de juntas).
We need a CEO who can navigate the company through these ____ waters. (Tiempos difíciles / Aguas turbulentas).
questions.explanation: Turbulent waters / times = tiempos turbulentos, inestables.

questions.question: The ____-Suite. (Ejecutivos nivel C)
The ____ of Directors. (Junta directiva con B)
A ____ takeover. (Adquisición hostil con H)
A ____ parachute. (Indemnización millonaria dorada)
Massive ____. (Despidos masivos con L)
____ company. (Empresa matriz con P)
To ____ the CEO. (Destituir con O)
Due ____. (Auditoría previa / Diligencia debida con D)
A ____ executive. (Ejecutivo experimentado/veterano con S)
A ____. (Fusión con M)
